name: Solid Pink
lede: Solid Pink is a dark, dusty rose-red so close to Deep Rose Red that our graph treats the two as the same color, and its own naming is undocumented beyond a bare Wikipedia listing.

sections.title: An undocumented name, a near-duplicate
sections.body: Wikipedia lists this as one of its web-sourced color names, and our library notes its origin as simply obscure: a qualified or novelty name with no traceable history in the books we checked [1]. By real look-alike distance it is a near-duplicate of [[deep-rose-red]] — essentially the same color under two different names — and it also neighbors [[peony-red]] and [[vandyke-red]], with [[bordeaux]] a little further out, duller and darker [2]. In English print the phrase 'solid pink' itself is comparatively recent, peaking and rising fastest in the 1950s, by Google Books' count across every sense of the words [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this rose-red in 84 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.35 percent, as photographed, more common than 52 percent of the named colors we track [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 0.7 percent of the 1,674 paintings we have from then (11 paintings), 2.1 times the museums' expected rate, and plays an accent in 74 percent of its appearances [4]. The earliest match is Hans Memling's 1470 painting, with the latest from 1947, fifty-one dated paintings in all — a floor, not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4].

origin.named_after: undocumented; Wikipedia lists it without explaining the name
